data: How do we make sense of India? Is India a rich country with poor people? Is it a scientific superpower or a land of superstition? Answering these questions requires an understanding of the contemporary history of India. We will first look through the first fifty-three years of Indian independence to see how different political parties rose and fell, how society and the environment have shaped politics, how India’s foreign policy is made and how the leadership styles of different Indian Prime Ministers varied. We will study a wide variety of important personalities including Jawaharlal Nehru, the Dalai Lama, Lalu Prasad Yadav, Salman Khan and Amartya Sen. We will also look at interesting changes in Indian history from the writing of the constitution to the 1962 Sino-Indian war to the rise of McDonalds. The course will be of interest to students of Indian history, politics and society. More broadly it will be of interest to anyone who is interested in the historical events that defined the lives of their parents and grandparents.
